# the contributor audit of the all-dimensional exponential entropy identity

Source: `candidate c324e86ba3893a31`.


Eliminating Y_j from the delta constraint has exact Jacobian1/|c_j|.
The conditional law of the other d variables has the stated cone
C and density exp(-beta.z)/Z with Z=|c_j|f_V(0). On C,
beta.z=sum Y_i>=sum_(i!=j)z_i. This proves finiteness, exponential
domination, and strictly positive finite coordinate means. The cone
has interior because the cut has both signs. No positivity of every
individual beta_i is needed outside C.

The radial decomposition Y=G Xi weights the independent Gamma(d+1)
law by1/G on conditioning V=0. The resulting Gamma(d) radial mean d
and uniform section angular law give means mu_i=d b_i exactly.
Cone homogeneity gives Z(s beta)=s^(-d)Z(beta); differentiation near
s=1 is justified by the same exponential bound, yielding beta.mu=d.

Relative entropy against the product exponentials with means mu_i
therefore equals log(product mu_i/Z), since both linear expectation
terms equal d. The elementary log inequality proves its nonnegativity,
including the missing mass of the reference density outside C.
If any other raw coordinate has the selected sign, that missing mass
is strictly positive, giving strictness. If none does, C is the full
orthant and the conditional law is itself the specified product,
giving equality. Zero other coefficients and d1 are included.

This establishes d^d product_(i!=j)b_i>=|c_j|f_V(0), with the exact
entropy deficit and correct scale invariance. It does NOT establish
the stronger cap-variance product bound. The explicit c=(1,1,-10)
calculation has F(1-F)=2100/14641>1210/14641=f_V(0), so substituting
the latter for the former would leave a real missing entropy payment.
